title: Nmap Recon & Enumeration Against Metasploitable 2
description: Students perform a structured network reconnaissance and enumeration exercise against a deliberately vulnerable VM (Metasploitable 2) using Nmap and auxiliary Metasploit modules, documenting discovered services and potential attack vectors.
objective: Students will conduct a multi-stage network scan, identify open services with version information, execute relevant NSE scripts, and produce a structured findings document that maps each service to a potential vulnerability.

steps.title: Environment Setup & Host Discovery
steps.instructions:
Boot Metasploitable 2 in VirtualBox/VMware on a host-only network. From your Kali attack VM, confirm connectivity and discover the target.

```bash
# Identify your attack machine's IP
ip addr show eth0

# Ping sweep to confirm target is alive
nmap -sn 192.168.56.0/24

# Confirm target responds
ping -c 3 <METASPLOITABLE_IP>
```

Record the Metasploitable IP address. Substitute it for `<TARGET>` in all subsequent commands.

steps.title: Full Port Scan with Service Version Detection
steps.instructions:
Run a comprehensive scan covering all TCP ports with service and version detection. Save output in all formats.

```bash
# Full port scan - may take 5-10 minutes
nmap -sS -sV -p- -T4 <TARGET> -oA /root/lab07/full_scan

# View results
cat /root/lab07/full_scan.nmap
```

**Expected findings to document:**
- Port 21 (FTP — vsftpd 2.3.4)
- Port 22 (SSH — OpenSSH)
- Port 23 (Telnet)
- Port 80 (HTTP — Apache)
- Port 3306 (MySQL)
- Port 5432 (PostgreSQL)
- Port 6667 (IRC — UnrealIRCd)
- Port 8180 (Apache Tomcat)

Create a table in your notes listing: Port | Service | Version | Risk Level.

steps.title: OS Fingerprinting and Default Script Scan
steps.instructions:
Run Nmap's OS detection and default scripts against discovered open ports.

```bash
# OS fingerprinting + default scripts on key ports
nmap -sC -O -p 21,22,23,80,139,445,3306,5432,6667,8180 <TARGET> -oN /root/lab07/scripts_scan.txt

# View the output
cat /root/lab07/scripts_scan.txt
```

Note observations:
- Does the FTP service allow anonymous login? (check ftp-anon script output)
- What SMB shares are visible? (check smb-enum-shares output)
- What OS does Nmap guess for the target?

steps.title: Targeted NSE Vulnerability Scripts
steps.instructions:
Run vulnerability-category NSE scripts to identify known CVEs on discovered services.

```bash
# Run vulnerability scripts (takes several minutes)
nmap --script vuln -p 21,23,80,139,445,3306,6667 <TARGET> -oN /root/lab07/vuln_scan.txt

# Also run specific high-value scripts
nmap --script ftp-vsftpd-backdoor -p 21 <TARGET>
nmap --script smb-vuln-ms17-010 -p 445 <TARGET>
nmap --script http-shellshock -p 80 <TARGET>
```

Document each vulnerability found:
- Script name
- CVE number (if provided)
- Description of the vulnerability
- CVSS score (look it up on nvd.nist.gov)

steps.title: Findings Documentation & Attack Surface Map
steps.instructions:
Compile your findings into a structured attack surface document.

```bash
# Generate XML output for structured parsing
nmap -sV -p- <TARGET> -oX /root/lab07/final_scan.xml

# Optional: convert to HTML for readable report
xsltproc /usr/share/nmap/nmap.xsl /root/lab07/final_scan.xml -o /root/lab07/report.html
```

**Your submission document must include:**
1. Network diagram (hand-drawn or draw.io) showing Kali → Metasploitable
2. Findings table: Port | Service | Version | CVE | CVSS | Priority
3. Top 3 recommended attack paths with justification
4. Screenshots of: host discovery, full scan, and at least one vuln script result

Prioritise the vsftpd backdoor (CVE-2011-2523) and UnrealIRCd backdoor (CVE-2010-2075) as high-impact targets for Lab 07-B.

expected_output: A PDF lab report containing: network diagram, findings table (minimum 8 services documented with CVE references), attack surface analysis, and screenshots of each nmap scan. XML scan output file attached.
